summary: Cognee notebook cell execution endpoint passes request bodies to exec(), allowing remote code execution
description:
Cognee 0.3.0 through 1.1.3 exposes a notebook cell execution API endpoint, POST /api/v1/notebooks/{notebook_id}/{cell_id}/run, that passes the request body to Python's exec() without sandboxing or validation (cognee/modules/notebooks/operations/run_in_local_sandbox.py). 

The endpoint was part of the local notebook UI and was intended for trusted local use, but it was exposed on the same network API surface and with the same authentication as the rest of the server, without sandboxing.

In releases before 1.1.0 the default configuration did not require authentication, so any network client could execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the server process; from 1.1.0 an authenticated user was required. 

The endpoint and the module containing the exec() call were removed before the 1.2.0 release (commits f258c631bd909737e53301626fadebec0cf81113 and 52bcc7494d026fc8a931af2cbfc2a0d883e80c23).

Versions 1.2.0 and later are not affected.

cwes.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code
